standard_prerequisites.use: The conclusion of the lemma is a pro-isomorphism of two inverse systems in D(A); this is the ambient framework in which the two comparison arrows are formed.

core_obligations: Construct the evident morphism of inverse systems from (M --f^n--> M) to (Coker(f^n)) inside D(A) (proof line 10047).

Under the stabilization hypothesis M[f^c] = M[f^(c+1)] = ... use the displayed diagrams with vertical maps f^c to build the reverse arrow of inverse systems, whose top level M/M[f^c] -> M is multiplication by f^(n+c) (proof lines 10048-10057).

Justify that these are inverse systems up to quasi-isomorphism: the top horizontal arrow is injective, so the top-row complex is quasi-isomorphic to Coker(f^(n+c)), yielding the claimed pro-isomorphism (proof lines 10058-10060).
proof_roadmap: Record the forward map from the first inverse system to the second.
Use stabilization at c to assemble the reverse arrow of inverse systems from the f^c maps in the diagram.
Identify the top row with the cokernel system via injectivity and conclude pro-isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts pro-isomorphism in the derived category of two inverse systems attached to an endomorphism f of an object M of an abelian category, under stabilization of the kernels M[f^n]. The forward comparison is immediate, but the reverse arrow has to be manufactured from the stabilization: each level M/M[f^c] -> M is multiplication by f^(n+c), and both the compatibility of this arrow with the two systems and the identification of the top row with Coker(f^(n+c)) via injectivity are the non-routine steps (proof lines 10048-10060). H2: no construction beyond a diagram, but the diagrammatic comparison inside D(A) is what a reader would be likely to miss.
